headline: Strong volumes offset input costs as buyback cuts shares
summary_short: Coca-Cola Consolidated's fiscal Q1 2026 net sales rose 16.9% y/y to $1,847M (+8.5% excluding six extra fiscal days), while diluted shares fell ~24% after a $2.40B November 2025 share Repurchase, lifting diluted EPS 40.7% to $1.67 even as net income grew a more modest 7.7%.
summary_long: Net sales grew 16.9% y/y to $1,847M (+8.5% adjusted for six extra fiscal days), on 13.4% volume growth and pricing actions. Gross margin fell 30bps to 39.4% on aluminum-cost and tariff inflation (~$35M). Operating income grew 25.1% to $238M, but interest expense jumped to $32.1M (from $6.9M) on debt raised for the November 2025 $2.40B Repurchase of 18.8M shares from a Coca-Cola Company affiliate, holding net income growth to 7.7% ($112M) while diluted EPS rose 40.7% to $1.67 on the shrunk share count. Cash fell to $233M after $150M of debt repayment; equity is now a $643M deficit. FY2026 capex guided to ~$300M; quarterly dividend held at $0.25/share.

drivers.explanation: Net sales grew on 13.4% volume growth and pricing actions, plus six extra fiscal days (~$132M impact) from the shifted fiscal calendar and an Easter-holiday shift; stripping the extra days, adjusted growth was 8.5%.
Gross margin fell 30bps to 39.4% as higher aluminum costs — from geopolitical conflicts, supply constraints and elevated import tariffs — added about $35M of input cost that outpaced pricing actions.

Operating income rose 25.1% to $238M as gross-profit gains outpaced a $52.3M SD&A increase, about $25M of which reflects the six extra fiscal days plus a $10M favorable non-cash fuel-hedge fair-value adjustment.

Operating margin expanded because operating income grew faster (+25.1%) than revenue (+16.9%) — arithmetic leverage from the extra-day and pricing gains outpacing the aluminum-cost and SD&A increases this quarter.

Net income grew just 7.7% versus operating income's 25.1% because interest expense jumped to $32.1M from $6.9M on debt raised for the November 2025 $2.40B Repurchase, plus a $53.4M non-cash mark-to-market charge.
Net margin fell to 6.0% from 6.6% because net income grew only 7.7% while revenue grew 16.9% — arithmetic dilution from the interest-expense and mark-to-market drag outpacing top-line gains.

Basic EPS grew 41.4% versus net income's 7.7% because weighted-average Common shares fell to 56.5M from 77.1M after the Company retired 18.8 million shares in the November 2025 $2.40B Repurchase from a Coca-Cola Company affiliate.
Diluted EPS grew 40.7% for the same reason as basic EPS — diluted weighted-average Common shares fell to 66.6M from 87.3M following the same November 2025 share Repurchase.

Cash fell 79.8% y/y almost entirely due to the November 2025 $2.40B Repurchase of 18.8 million shares from a Coca-Cola Company affiliate, funded by cash on hand plus new term-loan debt — not an operating decline.

This is a 10-Q, not an earnings press release, so no CEO/CFO commentary is included; the document's dominant narrative is the November 2025 $2.40B Repurchase of Seller shares, which reshaped the balance sheet, share count and EPS this quarter.
